land.text: a strip round Opole split from the Silesian duchy for Jarosław in 1172 (infobox 'Preceded by the Duchy of Silesia'; 'partitioned from Wrocław in 1172')

predecessors.note: The page gives no boundary for the 1172 duchy. Mieszko Tanglefoot's separate Racibórz (with Cieszyn) was split off in the same year and joined Opole only in 1202.

land.text: the Opole lands as a fiefdom of Bohemia: infobox 'Fiefdom of Bohemia (1291–1306; 1327–1348)', 'Fiefdom of the Bohemian Crown (until 1742)'

successors.note: Not a conquest and not an end of the duchy: Cliopatria's Opole row simply stops in 1304. The page has the duchy under its Piast dukes until Jan II the Good died without issue in 1532, when it reverted to the Bohemian Crown; Prussia took it in 1742. The Duchy of Opole after 1304 is not drawn by this dossier (see notes).

capitals.name: Opole
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Opole'; the page gives no coordinates, these are the gazetteer's Opole. Racibórz was a second seat of the Piast dukes of Racibórz (1172-1202, again from 1281) and is not recorded as a capital of this state.

rulers.name: Jarosław
rulers.note: First duke (Opole page); Bishop of Wrocław from 1198; died 22 March 1201 (Mieszko Tanglefoot page); the lands reverted to his father Bolesław of Silesia (Opole page).

rulers.name: Mieszko IV Tanglefoot
rulers.note: Duke of Racibórz from 1173, took Opole in 1202 and merged it with Racibórz; High Duke at Kraków from 9 June 1210; died 16 May 1211 (Mieszko Tanglefoot page). Silesian rule over Opole between March and December 1201 is not listed.

rulers.name: Casimir I
rulers.note: Duke of Opole-Racibórz 1211-1230; died 13 May 1230 (Casimir I of Opole page).

rulers.name: Mieszko II the Fat
rulers.note: Duke from 1230 to his death on 22 October 1246; under the guardianship of Henry I the Bearded and then (1238-39) the regency of Henry II the Pious; the page does not date when he took over ('probably in late 1238 or early 1239').

rulers.name: Władysław of Opole
rulers.note: Racibórz page list 'Władysław of Opole (1246–1281)'; the Opole page puts his death in 1281 ('After the death of Mieszko's grandson Duke Władysław Opolski in 1281'), the Bolko I page in 1282 (his own article could not be read: url_not_found, tried Władysław_Opolski, W%C5%82adys%C5%82aw_Opolski, Władysław_I_of_Opole). In 1241-1244 he held Kalisz (Mieszko II page).

rulers.name: Bolko I (with his brother Casimir of Bytom to 1284)
rulers.note: Bolko I page: Duke of Opole 'with Casimir (until 1284) 1282–1313' (infobox), co-ruler with Casimir for two years until the formal division of 1284, then alone with Opole, Niemodlin and Strzelce Opolskie; died 14 May 1313. The strip starts in 1281 because the Opole page dates the recreation of the duchy to 1281; it stops at this dossier's end in 1304, not at his death.

correction.text: the Opole lands of Duke Jarosław, 1172-1200: 'the Duchy of Opole was formed with Jarosław becoming the first duke'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the page forms the duchy in 1172 (infobox 'partitioned from Wrocław in 1172'), five years before Cliopatria's first shape. The page gives the duchy no boundary; the correction draws the Opole lands as a 45 km disc round the capital (about 6,600 km2, the same size as Cliopatria's 6,536 km2) and is the researcher's reading. The Duchy of Opole infobox has no Area line, so the area comparison could not be made.

correction.text: the Opole lands of Duke Jarosław (1172-1200); Cliopatria's shape here is Mieszko Tanglefoot's separate Racibórz-Cieszyn duchy, which joined Opole only in 1202

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria's 1177-1201 shape (6,536 km2, 49.45-50.38 N) lies south of Opole: a gazetteer check finds Racibórz, Cieszyn and Gliwice inside it and Opole city outside. The Mieszko Tanglefoot page says that after the 1172 rebellion Bolesław 'was forced to give separate lands to both Mieszko (who received the towns of Racibórz and Cieszyn)', and the Racibórz page has a separate 'Duchy of Racibórz ... formed in 1172 as a territory for Mieszko'. So the shape is Mieszko's Racibórz, not Jarosław's Opole; it belongs to the united duchy only from 1202. For 1177-1200 the Opole lands are drawn as in the 1172 keyframe; in March 1201 they revert to Silesia (ledger). The Duchy of Opole infobox has no Area line, so the area comparison could not be made.

correction.text: the merged Duchy of Opole and Racibórz from 1202; the shape Cliopatria draws from 1206, applied from 1202

keyframe_review.note: Right years for the merger ('in 1202 Opole was taken by ... Mieszko I Tanglefoot of Racibórz, who merged it with his duchy'; infobox 'united with Racibórz in 1202') but the shape (6,714 km2) is still only the Racibórz-Cieszyn lands: Opole city is outside it (gazetteer check). Cliopatria's 1206 shape (12,710 km2, Opole plus Racibórz, Bytom, Cieszyn and Gliwice) is the union and applies from 1202. The Duchy of Opole infobox has no Area line, so the area comparison could not be made.

12,710 km2: Opole with the Racibórz lands (Racibórz, Cieszyn, Gliwice and Bytom fall inside by a gazetteer check). The Racibórz page has the duchy united with Opole in 1202, so the shape is right for 1206-1209 and applies from 1202 (see the 1202 verdict). The Duchy of Opole infobox has no Area line, so the area comparison could not be made.

correction.text: the merged Opole-Racibórz duchy and Kraków, 1210-1211 only: 'left him in total control over the capital without fighting'; the page names no other land

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria's 1210-1215 shape (95,164 km2, 16.7-22.0 E, 49.2-54.9 N, with Kraków, Sieradz, Konin and Włocławek inside by a gazetteer check) is Mieszko Tanglefoot as High Duke. The page has him 'Duke of Kraków and High Duke of Poland: from 9 June 1210 until his death one year later' (16 May 1211) and gives only Kraków itself; nothing on the page puts Greater Poland or Kuyavia in his hands. So 1210-1211 is the merged duchy plus Kraków; from 1212 (Casimir I, who 'took over his father's Opole and Racibórz duchies') it is the merged duchy alone (next keyframe). The Duchy of Opole infobox has no Area line, so the area comparison could not be made.

correction.text: the Opole-Racibórz duchy of Casimir I, 1212-1215

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1212-1215: after Mieszko's death 'Casimir then took over his father's Opole and Racibórz duchies' (Casimir I page, 'Duke of Opole-Racibórz, 1211–1230'); the page gives him no Kraków and no Greater Polish land, so the Cliopatria 1216 shape (12,710 km2) is applied to the four years.

correction.text: unchanged: the Opole-Racibórz duchy, holding 1216-1233 only

keyframe_review.note: 12,710 km2, the same extent as 1206-1209, right for 1216-1233 (Casimir I 1211-1230, then his sons under guardianship). Only the years change: Kalisz and Wieluń come in 1234 (Mieszko II page), two years before Cliopatria's 1236 shape; Casimir's 1227 annexation of Czeladź is too small to show. Shape unchanged, holds 1216-1233. The Duchy of Opole infobox has no Area line, so the area comparison could not be made.

correction.text: the Opole-Racibórz duchy with Kalisz and Wieluń, from 1234

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1234-1235: 'A year later [after the 1233 bull], to calm the erupted rebellion against this decision,' Henry I gave Kalisz and Wieluń to Casimir's sons; the infobox dates Mieszko's rule there to 1234-1239. Cliopatria's 1236 shape (22,526 km2, with Kalisz, Wieluń and Sieradz inside by a gazetteer check) is applied two years earlier.

22,526 km2 (shapes.csv 1236-1240): the Opole-Racibórz core plus Kalisz and Wieluń (a gazetteer check finds Kalisz, Wieluń and Sieradz inside). The Mieszko II page dates the grant to 1234 and ends Mieszko's rule at Kalisz and Wieluń in 1239 ('Duke of Kalisz 1234–1239', 'Duke of Wieluń 1234–1239'), and the Henry II the Pious page has Henry retaining Kalisz and Wieluń in 1239. Shape unchanged, holds 1236-1238; 1239-1240 is the next keyframe. The Duchy of Opole infobox has no Area line, so the area comparison could not be made.

correction.text: unchanged: the Opole-Racibórz duchy with Kalisz and Wieluń, holding 1236-1238 only
the Opole-Racibórz core without Kalisz and Wieluń, 1239-1240: Henry II 'managed to retain Greater Polish Kalisz and Wieluń'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1239-1240, replacing the last two years of Cliopatria's 1236 shape: Kalisz and Wieluń are back with Silesia (ledger 1239) until Władysław is given Kalisz in 1241. The core is Cliopatria's 1216 shape (12,710 km2). Kalisz 1239-1241 is the reviewer's thin finding; the pages do not name the holder of Wieluń in 1239-1240 beyond Henry II retaining it.

correction.text: the Opole-Racibórz duchy with Kalisz and Wieluń, 1241-1243

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria's 1241-1249 shape (18,092 km2) leaves Opole city outside (gazetteer check) while keeping Kalisz and Wieluń to 1249; the page has the opposite: 'In 1241 Władysław ... was declared an adult ... receiving Kalisz', then 'in 1244, Władysław was forced to withdraw from Kalisz', keeping only Wieluń, which he lost in 1249. So 1241-1243 is the 1236 shape (core, Kalisz, Wieluń); 1244-1248 the core plus Wieluń; 1249 the core (next keyframes). Mieszko II's 1246 will gave 'all of his lands to his brother Władysław, except the district of Cieszyn', left to their mother Viola as dower; that dower stays drawn as Opole land (an internal grant, no change of state). The Duchy of Opole infobox has no Area line, so the area comparison could not be made. Repair pass: Władysław holds Kalisz from the 1241 grant by Henry II the Pious (ledger 1241), so the shape is right from 1241.

correction.text: the Opole-Racibórz core with Wieluń, 1244-1248: 'forced to withdraw from Kalisz', keeping only Wieluń

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1244-1248: Kalisz is lost in 1244 ('Władysław was forced to withdraw from Kalisz') and Wieluń is kept until 1249. The Wieluń disc is the researcher's reading of 'Wieluń'.

correction.text: the Opole-Racibórz core after the loss of Wieluń, 1249

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for the single year 1249, when Wieluń is lost (the page: 'which he lost in 1249 (per the page)'); the shape is Cliopatria's 1250 core, applied one year early.

12,997 km2 by shapes.csv (the gazetteer's cell count gives 14,162 km2; that is the cell rasterisation, not a second figure): the Opole-Racibórz core under Władysław (1246-1281). Cieszyn is inside; the district was Viola's dower after 1246 (Mieszko II page; Viola d. 7 September 1251 per the Casimir I page). Nothing on the pages opened contradicts the shape for 1250-1271 (unverified beyond that: page budget; Władysław's own page could not be read). The Duchy of Opole infobox has no Area line, so the area comparison could not be made.

correction.text: unchanged: the Opole-Racibórz duchy, holding 1272-1280 only

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria's 1272-1284 shape (12,217 km2) drops Cieszyn but still holds Racibórz, Gliwice and Bytom; none of the pages opened explains the 1272 loss of Cieszyn (unverified: page budget). The page splits Racibórz off in 1281, so the shape holds for 1272-1280 and the 1285 shape applies from 1281 (next keyframe). The Duchy of Opole infobox has no Area line, so the area comparison could not be made. Repair pass: the Duchy of Cieszyn page starts its story with the 1281 split ('split off the Silesian Duchy of Opole and Racibórz in 1281'; the Racibórz branch 'initially ruled the Duchy of Racibórz with Cieszyn and Oświęcim') and is silent on who held Cieszyn in 1246-1280 and on any 1270-1272 event, so the 1272 cut stays unexplained.

correction.text: the Duchy of Opole recreated for Casimir and Bolko I, 1281-1283: the 1285 Opole shape plus the Gliwice-Koźle lands of Cliopatria's Bytom shape, which Casimir takes only in 1284; without Racibórz, Cieszyn and the Bytom disc

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1281-1283: 'After the death of Mieszko's grandson Duke Władysław Opolski in 1281, his sons again divided the Duchy of Opole and Racibórz'; 'the Duchy of Opole was recreated for Casimir and his brother Bolko I, contemporaneously with the establishment of the duchies of Cieszyn and Bytom on former Racibórz territory'; infobox 'Split off Racibórz: 1281'. The Bolko I page has the brothers ruling Opole jointly (1282 to 1284 on that page) until the formal division of 1284, and the Bytom dossier draws only a 15 km disc round Bytom for 1281-1283, so the rest of Cliopatria's Bytom shape (Gliwice, Koźle) stays in Opole's hands until 1284 (about 8,350 km2 in all). Cliopatria shows the smaller Opole only from 1285. The Racibórz page says Racibórz was 'recreated again' in 1290. Repair of reviewer finding 3 (previously 1281-1284 with the 1285 shape alone).

correction.text: Opole after the formal division of 1284: Bolko I 'kept Opole', Casimir received Bytom

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for the single year 1284, when the domains are formally divided (Bolko I page); the shape is Cliopatria's 1285 Opole shape (6,637 km2) applied one year early. The Opole page does not mention 1284.

6,637 km2: Opole proper (the shape minus Cliopatria's Duchy of Bytom 1285 shape keeps 6,575 km2, so the overlap with Bytom is only about 60 km2). Right in extent for the recreated duchy; it applies from 1284 (previous keyframe), not 1285. From 17 January 1291 Opole is a Bohemian fief (ledger 1291; infobox 'Fiefdom of Bohemia (1291–1306; 1327–1348)'); the page's text has 'Vassalized (finally) by Bohemia: 1327'. The Duchy of Opole infobox has no Area line, so the area comparison could not be made.

6,637 km2, identical to 1285; nothing on the pages opened changes Opole's borders between 1285 and 1304 (the Bolko I page names Opole, Niemodlin and Strzelce Opolskie as his core lands and adds Wieluń only in 1305). Opole is a fiefdom of Bohemia from 1291 (ledger); Cliopatria's row ends in 1304 although the duchy lived on (see the dissolve event). The Duchy of Opole infobox has no Area line, so the area comparison could not be made.

region.text: the Opole lands of Duke Jarosław

ledger.note: 1172: after a long dispute the Duchy of Opole is formed under Duke Jarosław. 'After a long-term dispute in 1172 the Duchy of Opole was formed with Jarosław becoming the first duke'; infobox 'partitioned from Wrocław in 1172', 'Capital: Opole'. The page gives the duchy no boundary (the region is a disc round the capital), and Mieszko Tanglefoot's Racibórz was formed beside it the same year.

region.text: the Opole lands, reverted to Bolesław of Silesia (drawn as Silesian from 1201 until Mieszko's seizure in 1202, whatever the 1177 keyframe's span says)

ledger.note: 1201: Jarosław dies and Opole falls back to Silesia. 'When Duke Jarosław died in 1201, the Opole lands reverted to his still living father Bolesław'; the Mieszko Tanglefoot page dates Jarosław's death to 22 March 1201 and Bolesław's to 7/8 December 1201 (his lands passed to Henry the Bearded).

region.text: the Opole lands taken from Silesia

ledger.note: 1202: Mieszko Tanglefoot seizes Opole. 'in 1202 Opole was taken by his brother [sic: Jarosław's uncle] Duke Mieszko I Tanglefoot of Racibórz, who merged it with his duchy'; the Mieszko Tanglefoot page has 'a surprise attack at the beginning of 1202' and 'Duke of Opole from 1202'. The page does not name the holder he took it from; Henry the Bearded, Bolesław's heir, is implied (Silesia dossier mirrors the loss).

region.text: Mieszko's own duchy of Racibórz with Cieszyn, joined to the Opole lands

ledger.note: 1202: Racibórz and Opole are united. 'In 1202 Mieszko occupied the Duchy of Opole of his deceased nephew Jarosław', after which the page treats the two as one; the Opole infobox says 'united with Racibórz in 1202'. The region is Cliopatria's 1203 shape, which a gazetteer check puts on Racibórz, Cieszyn and Gliwice (the Mieszko Tanglefoot page: Mieszko 'received the towns of Racibórz and Cieszyn'); Cliopatria itself draws the union only from 1206.

region.text: Kraków and its lands, the seniorate seat

ledger.note: 1210: Mieszko Tanglefoot takes Kraków and the High Duke's title. 'Duke of Kraków and High Duke of Poland: from 9 June 1210 until his death one year later'; 'the confusion among the citizens left him in total control over the capital without fighting', after Innocent III's bull of 9 June 1210 deposed and excommunicated the seniorate rulers including Leszek the White. The page does not say whom he displaced or which land came with Kraków; the Sandomierz dossier mirrors the loss. Cliopatria's much larger 1210 shape is not supported (see the 1210 verdict).

1211: Mieszko dies and Kraków passes back to Leszek the White. Mieszko died on 16 May 1211; 'Only after Mieszko's death could Leszek the White return to Kraków without major difficulties'. Casimir I then 'took over his father's Opole and Racibórz duchies' (Casimir I page).

1227: Casimir I annexes Czeladź. 'in 1227 as a result of the confusion reigning in Poland following the death of High Duke Leszek I the White, Casimir annexed Czeladź.' The page names no holder; Leszek's Kraków-Sandomierz lands (the Sandomierz dossier) are the likely loser. A small town district, too small to show in the 1216 shape.

1234: Henry the Bearded gives Kalisz and Wieluń to Casimir's sons. 'A year later [after the 1233 bull of Gregory IX], to calm the erupted rebellion against this decision,' Henry I gave these lands to Casimir's sons; infobox: Mieszko's rule at Kalisz and Wieluń 1234-1239, shared with Władysław. Henry I's Silesia took Kalisz from Greater Poland in 1234 (Greater Poland and Silesia dossiers), so the lands pass on from Silesia.

region.text: Opole-Racibórz under Henry I's 'full control ... but without denying their hereditary rights'

ledger.note: 1234: Henry the Bearded takes full control of Opole-Racibórz as guardian of Casimir I's sons. Mieszko II page, in the passage on the 1234 grant of Kalisz and Wieluń: Henry I was 'taking the full control over Opole-Racibórz, but without denying their hereditary rights'. The regency had been shared with the boys' mother since 1230 and passed at Henry I's death in 1238 to Henry II the Pious, 'who also assumed the regency over Opole-Racibórz'. A guardianship, not a feudal vassalage; it is recorded as the nearest level of rule 4 because the dukes kept their hereditary rights. The counterpart is the overlord, as in a vassal's own ledger. Silesia's ledger has this as a 1234 'gain' of Opole (/ledger/15) and a 1239 'loss' (/ledger/18); both should become the mirror vassal_start and vassal_end. Repair of reviewer finding 2.

region.text: Opole-Racibórz as Mieszko II takes over its rule

ledger.note: 1239: the Silesian guardianship ends. Mieszko II page: 'It is unknown exactly when Mieszko II took over the rule over Opole-Racibórz', most likely 'late 1238 or early 1239'; the Henry II the Pious page (second page): 'in 1239, Henry was compelled to resign the regency'. The year is the pages'; whether it was late 1238 or early 1239 is not settled. Repair of reviewer finding 2.

1239: Kalisz and Wieluń go back to Silesia. Henry II the Pious page: despite losing the regency he 'managed to retain Greater Polish Kalisz and Wieluń'; the Mieszko II infobox ends Mieszko's rule there in 1239 ('Duke of Kalisz 1234–1239', 'Duke of Wieluń 1234–1239'). The Mieszko II page also has his mother Viola and Władysław 'expected to remain in Kalisz, which held power under the guidance of the Duke of Wrocław' (undated, about 1239). The year is the pages'; that the lands pass wholly to Silesia, and not merely under its guidance, is my reading. Silesia's ledger has no mirror (it should show a 1239 gain of Kalisz and Wieluń). Closes the thin finding on Kalisz 1239-1241.

region.text: the Duchy of Kalisz given to Władysław

ledger.note: 1241: Władysław receives Kalisz from Henry II. 'In 1241 Władysław, Mieszko II's younger brother, was declared an adult and able to govern' and 'was satisfied with the Duchy of Kalisz given to him by Henry II the Pious'. The page does not say Wieluń came with the grant; it first names Wieluń in 1244 ('maintaining only his rule over Wieluń'), so Wieluń is drawn with Kalisz from 1241 (my reading, hence confidence 2). The Silesia ledger has no matching 1241 loss to Opole.

1244: Władysław is forced out of Kalisz. 'in 1244, Władysław was forced to withdraw from Kalisz', keeping only Wieluń. The page does not say who took it; the Greater Poland dossier records Kalisz regained in 1244 (counterpart given there as Silesia), the page says only that the Greater Polish dukes wanted it back (undated). After the 1241 grant by Henry II the Pious Kalisz was Władysław's, so the taker's mirror in the Greater Poland dossier (gain 1244, counterpart given there as duchy-of-silesia) should name duchy-of-opole.
1249: Wieluń is lost. Władysław kept Wieluń after 1244, 'which he lost in 1249 (per the page)'. The page names no taker; the Greater Poland dossier mirrors the gain of Wieluń in 1249.

region.text: Racibórz, split off in 1281 (the Racibórz dossier's own land)

ledger.note: 1281: Racibórz is split off again after Duke Władysław's death. 'After the death of Mieszko's grandson Duke Władysław Opolski in 1281, his sons again divided the Duchy of Opole and Racibórz'; infobox 'Split off Racibórz: 1281'. The Bolko I page has Racibórz going to the brothers Mieszko I and Przemysław. The Racibórz page lists Przemysław from 1281 and says the duchy was 'recreated again' in 1290; Cliopatria's Racibórz shape begins 1285. Repair pass: the region is now Cliopatria's Racibórz 1285 shape (the mirror's land), not the 1275 shape minus the 1285 Opole shape, which also held the Bytom lands (split off separately in the next event). That difference leaves two cells (about 506 km2, the western and eastern fringes of the 1275 shape) that neither Racibórz nor Bytom draws.

region.text: Bytom, established as a duchy on former Racibórz land; the page gives no extent before the 1284 division

ledger.note: 1281: the Duchy of Bytom is established beside the recreated Opole. 'the Duchy of Opole was recreated for Casimir and his brother Bolko I, contemporaneously with the establishment of the duchies of Cieszyn and Bytom on former Racibórz territory'. The region is only the 15 km disc round Bytom that the Bytom dossier draws as its 1281 land. The Gliwice-Koźle lands of Cliopatria's Bytom 1285 shape stay with Opole until the formal division of 1284 (next events; Bolko I page: Bolko and Casimir 'inherited Opole as co-rulers' and ruled together until 1284). Repair pass, 2026-11-01: previously the whole Bytom 1285 shape was split off here, which left Gliwice and Koźle drawn by no state in 1281-1283.

region.text: the Gliwice-Koźle lands of the Bytom duchy (Cliopatria's Bytom 1285 shape outside the 15 km disc round Bytom drawn from 1281)

ledger.note: 1284: Casimir's share is formally divided from Opole. Bolko I page (WebFetch summary): after Władysław's death Bolko and Casimir 'inherited Opole as co-rulers'; the common rule lasted two years, until 1284, when the domains were formally divided; Bolko kept Opole and Casimir received Bytom. The Bytom dossier (another group) dates Casimir's gain of Koźle, Toszek, Gliwice and Siewierz to 1284 and draws only a 15 km disc round Bytom for 1281-1283. The Opole page itself has the duchy 'recreated for Casimir and his brother Bolko I'. The region is the Bytom 1285 shape outside the disc; the towns are the Bytom dossier's. Repair of reviewer finding 3.

region.text: the Opole lands as a fiefdom of Bohemia

ledger.note: 17 January 1291: Opole's duke does homage to the Bohemian crown. Bolko I page (WebFetch summary): on 17 January 1291 at Olomouc Bolko, Mieszko I and Casimir agreed to fight the enemies of the Přemyslid dynasty and homage was performed to the Bohemian crown; some historians date the homage to 1292, and the page does not call it a fief. Duchy of Opole infobox (second page): 'Fiefdom of Bohemia (1291–1306; 1327–1348)', while its text has 'Vassalized (finally) by Bohemia: 1327' and 'In 1327 King John the Blind of Bohemia reasserted his influence'. The fief runs to 1306 (infobox; the Bolko page: the extinction of the Přemyslids in 1306 'broke the existing alliance'), after this dossier's end in 1304, so no vassal_end is recorded inside the life. The counterpart is the overlord; kingdom-of-bohemia has only the 1289 Bytom homage and needs the mirror vassal_start for Opole. Repair of reviewer finding 1.

region.text: the Opole lands as the shapes of record end; the duchy itself continues as a Bohemian fief

ledger.note: 1304: last year of Cliopatria's Opole shape, not the end of the duchy. The Opole page has the duchy a fiefdom of Bohemia 1291-1306 and 1327-1348, merged with Racibórz again in 1521 and extinct with Jan II the Good in 1532, when it 'reverted to the Bohemian Crown'. The Bolko I page has Bolko ruling Opole until his death on 14 May 1313, with Wieluń added in 1305 (infobox 'Duke of Wieluń 1305–1313'), and nothing on 1304. The dossier stops where the shapes stop; the period 1305-1532 needs its own keyframes (notes). Confidence 1: the year is Cliopatria's.

wars.name: Mieszko Tanglefoot's conquest of Opole
wars.outcome: Mieszko Tanglefoot of Racibórz takes Opole in a surprise attack at the beginning of 1202 and merges it with his duchy.
wars.note: 'Mieszko was determined to obtain Opole and made a surprise attack at the beginning of 1202'; Jarosław died 22 March 1201 and Bolesław 7/8 December 1201. No named war; no fighting is described.

wars.name: Mieszko Tanglefoot's seizure of Kraków
wars.outcome: Mieszko takes Kraków without fighting in 1210 and holds it until his death on 16 May 1211, after which Leszek the White returns.
wars.note: Papal bull of Innocent III, 9 June 1210, deposing the seniorate rulers; the page names Leszek only in the bull context.

wars.name: Henry I the Bearded's Kraków campaign
wars.outcome: Unsuccessful: Henry's expedition against Kraków failed, with Opole-Racibórz troops taking part.
wars.note: 'during the unsuccessful trip of Henry I the Bearded against Kraków in 1225'; the defender is not named on the page (Leszek the White held Kraków, Sandomierz dossier).

wars.name: Mongol invasion of Poland
wars.outcome: The Mongols raid Silesia in 1241 and defeat Henry II the Pious at Legnica on 9 April; Mieszko II fights part of them at Racibórz in March; no land changes hands.
wars.note: 'in March 1241 at the Battle of Raciborz Mieszko II managed to catch part of the Mongolian troops'; 'Already in May 1241, Mieszko II began the reconstruction of the devastated territories'.

wars.name: Konrad of Masovia's 1243 bid for Kraków
wars.outcome: Mieszko II supports his father-in-law Konrad I of Masovia against Kraków; their forces are defeated and no ground is won.
wars.note: 'In 1243, Mieszko II military supported his father-in-law Konrad I of Masovia'; the defenders are not named on the page.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line is given on any of the five pages; the duchy is a set of named castellanies and towns (Opole, Racibórz, Cieszyn, Bytom, Kalisz, Wieluń). The 1281 partition lines are not recorded; the Cliopatria cuts of 1202-1280 are approximate.

notes: Duchy of Opole, 5 pages opened (Opole, Mieszko IV Tanglefoot, Casimir I, Mieszko II the Fat, Racibórz; budget up to 5). 1) Cliopatria's Opole shapes before 1206 are Mieszko Tanglefoot's Racibórz-Cieszyn lands, not Opole: Opole city is outside the 1177-1205 shape (gazetteer check) and the Mieszko page gives Racibórz and Cieszyn to Mieszko in 1172. The dossier draws Jarosław's Opole as a 45 km disc round the capital for 1172-1200 (the researcher's reading, no page gives a boundary) and the merged duchy from 1202. The separate Duchy of Racibórz 1172-1202 has no dossier (duchy-of-raciborz starts 1281): the group's Racibórz agent should extend it back or the gap-filler should draw it. 2) The 1210-1215 shape (95,164 km2) is the High Duke seat; supported only for Kraków 1210-1211. 3) The 1241-1249 shape lacks Opole city; corrected from the Mieszko II page. 4) The page for Władysław Opolski (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/W%C5%82adys%C5%82aw_Opolski) returned url_not_found twice (also Władysław_Opolski unencoded and Vladislaus_of_Opole); his reign (1246-1281) rests on the Racibórz list and the Casimir I and Mieszko II pages. Bolko I of Opole was not opened: the 1285-1304 reigns, the 1289-1291 Bohemian homage and the 1297-1304 events are not covered. 5) Bohemian overlordship (infobox 'Fiefdom of Bohemia (1291–1306; 1327–1348)', page text 'Vassalized (finally) by Bohemia: 1327'; Racibórz page 1327) is a vassal_start for the kingdom-of-bohemia dossier, counterpart duchy-of-opole; it is not a ledger event here. 6) The Opole page says Opole was taken in 1202 by 'his brother' Mieszko; the Mieszko page makes him Jarosław's uncle (the Racibórz page: 'his deceased nephew Jarosław'). 7) Silesia's dossier has Henry I take 'direct control of Opole' in 1234; the Mieszko II page has the 1233 papal bull move the guardianship to the church and then Henry grant Kalisz and Wieluń in 1234; not reconciled. 8) The Cieszyn district: Mieszko II's will (1246) leaves it to Viola as dower (she died 7 September 1251); kept drawn as Opole land, no ledger event. Cliopatria drops Cieszyn from the 1272 shape with no page explaining it. 9) The dossier ends at 1304 with the Cliopatria row; the duchy continued to 1532 (page) and again 1645-1666 under the Vasas, but 1305-1532 (partitions of the Opole line, Bohemian fief 1327, merger with Racibórz 1521) needs another batch, as does the period 1285-1304. 10) No infobox area on any page opened, so no area comparison. Places missing from the gazetteer and used here: Kalisz, Wieluń, Czeladź (country Poland).
